summary: fix(concur): attach browser fallbacks to a Chrome whose remote debugging was enabled at chrome://inspect (DevToolsActivePort ws:// endpoint); correct the Chrome >= 136 setup docs
reason: Every browser fallback (expenses create/update, reports create/submit, hotels search) first tries to attach to an already-logged-in Chrome via `agent-browser --cdp <port>`. When Chrome's remote debugging was switched on at chrome://inspect, Chrome serves no DevTools HTTP discovery endpoints (/json/version answers 404), so that probe timed out, detection returned "", and the fallback silently launched an isolated, unauthenticated browser that failed with "not logged in" -- even with a logged-in Chrome listening on the conventional port. Chrome records its WebSocket endpoint in a DevToolsActivePort file (user-data directory root for the --remote-debugging-port flag, profile directory for the chrome://inspect toggle), and `agent-browser --cdp` accepts that ws:// URL directly (confirmed live). Separately, the documented setup (--remote-debugging-port with --profile-directory) is ignored by Chrome >= 136, which requires a non-default --user-data-dir for remote debugging; the help text and README told users to do something that no longer works. The detection probe also ran without --session, leaving an unnamed daemon attached to whichever browser it probed.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Discovering a Concur tab among several open tabs
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Detection keeps the existing contract that the attached browser's active tab is a signed-in Concur page. Scanning every tab would expose the titles and URLs of unrelated tabs in a user's everyday Chrome, so it was left out rather than guessed at.

validated_outcome: go build, go vet and go test ./... pass. Unit tests cover DevToolsActivePort parsing (CRLF, bad port, bad path, path traversal, whitespace), discovery in both the user-data-dir root and a profile subdirectory, loopback-only ws:// validation, that the session id never appears in messages or in agent-browser failure errors (argv and echoed stderr), probe ordering, skipping closed ports without spawning agent-browser, and that the probe passes `--cdp ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/devtools/browser/<id>`. Live: auto-detection of a dedicated debug Chrome on port 9333 was verified end to end (the amended `expenses update --type` attached without any separate login). Attaching with the ws:// endpoint of a chrome://inspect-enabled Chrome was verified by hand with agent-browser; the CLI's own pickup of that file is covered by unit tests only, because Chrome stopped publishing the file during testing.
